note: Attacker-controlled bytes enter the fuzz target as the raw UART payload.
The input is copied verbatim into a heap buffer that is then handed to the UART receive path.
The raw bytes are injected into the platform UART callback, which feeds the NCP parser and command handling logic.
The UART-driven NCP path can reach Thread network-data registration handling on the leader side.
Received network-data TLVs are passed into RegisterNetworkData with attacker-influenced contents and length.

note: The code compares new and existing network data to decide whether stable-version bookkeeping is needed.
When a stable service/server TLV is present, the code walks the base service's server list without a strict end-bound check on the current TLV pointer.
The sink reads server data using the attacker-controlled server-data length, which can overrun the current TLV and trigger the reported stack-buffer-overflow read.
